open_assumptions: What `claude --safe-mode` restricts, and that `--permission-mode dontAsk` with a single Edit(//path) allow rule denies every other reviewer write, are stated in code comments as observed live and asserted by no test.
The live `claude agents --json` state vocabulary (idle, working, blocked, done) is inferred from InteractiveSessions.locate and commit 3c7354c, not from CLI documentation.

LangGraph's handling of a parallel verify task killed by KeyboardInterrupt (whether the sibling's write is kept) and whether `retry` re-runs a node that raised after consuming an interrupt resume value are taken from the runbook, not from any test.
The out-of-band event in worker-lanes-001 (sequence 11) and the manual reset of attempt counters in two recorded runs are assumed to be operator edits; no repository history produces them.
The document's claim that a worker can push relies on the source repository's SSH origin and the account's keys; whether the keys are loaded in the worker's environment was not tested.
result.summary: Wrote docs/audit/WORKFLOW_AUDIT.md (749 lines): ten sections answering the operator's questions with path:line citations into workflow/automatic.py, pipeline.py, interactive.py, sessions.py, checks.py, verification.py, export_state.py, launch.py and server/projects.ts, the test class and method for every proven claim, explicit 'untested' marks, the recorded runs (parallel-reviewers-001 identical candidate attempts and out-of-tree relaunch from branch fix/worker-relaunch, worker-lanes-001 inventory failure and hand-reset attempts, parallel-reviewers-002), a table of every terminal condition with its message, and ten ranked recommendations. No other file changed. Checks executed in this worktree after npm ci: npm run test:contracts (18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail, exit 0) and npm run test:unit (130 tests, 130 pass, 0 fail, exit 0). The Python unittest suite was not run; test attributions come from reading the sources.
